عِبْرٌ , (S, O, K, TA, in the CK عِبْرَة,) and ↓ عُبْرٌ , (S, O,) or ↓ عَبْرٌ , (Kr, A, K, TA, accord. to the CK عَبْرَة,) The bank, or side, (S, A, O, K,) of a river, (S, A, O,) and of a valley. (A, K.) En-Nábighah Edh-Dhubyánee says, of the Euphrates, “تَرْمِى أَوَاذِيُّهُ العِبْرَيْنِ بِالزَّبَدِ
” [Its waves casting foam upon the two banks]. (S, O.) And one says, فُلَانٌ فِى ذٰلِكَ العِبْرِ Such a one is upon that side. (TA.) ＝
-A2- See also the next preceding paragraph, in three places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
